description: Synthetic published policy wordings for the retrieval evaluation. Gold v1 and v2 differ only in a few values, so that any leak between versions shows. Shield is longer, with the kinds of clauses a claim question needs. All text is fictional.

gold-v1: Sum Insured INR 5,00,000 per policy year. Co-payment 10% of each admissible claim where the Insured Person is aged 61 or above. Deductible Nil.
Hospitalization means admission to a Hospital for at least 24 consecutive in-patient care hours, except for Day Care Treatment as defined in Clause 1.2.
Day Care Treatment means a procedure completed in under 24 hours of admission because of technological advancement.
Pre-existing Disease means any condition diagnosed within 48 months before the first policy issued by the Insurer.
In-patient Hospitalization: up to Sum Insured. Subject to Clause 1.1.
Room rent: 1% of Sum Insured per day. Proportionate deduction applies if exceeded.
Intensive care unit: 2% of Sum Insured per day. Medically necessary admission only.
Pre-hospitalization: 30 days before admission. Related to the admitted condition.
Post-hospitalization: 60 days after discharge. Related to the admitted condition.
Cataract surgery: INR 40,000 per eye. See waiting period in Clause 3.2.
Ambulance: INR 2,500 per Hospitalization. Registered ambulance services only.
No claim is payable in the first 30 days of the policy, except for accidents.
A 24-month waiting period applies to cataract, hernia, joint replacement, and kidney stones, unless the condition arises from an accident.
Pre-existing Diseases, as defined in Clause 1.3, are covered after 36 months.
Cosmetic or aesthetic treatment, except reconstruction following an accident.
Treatment of obesity, unless the conditions of Clause 4.3 are all met.
Bariatric surgery is covered only if BMI is 40 or above, and advised by a doctor.
Non-medical items listed in Annexure A, such as toiletries and attendant charges.
Notify the Insurer within 48 hours of an emergency admission.
Submit documents within 30 days of discharge. Required: signed claim form, itemized hospital bill, discharge summary, and prescriptions and reports.

platinum: Sum Insured INR 7,50,000 per policy year. Deductible INR 25,000 per policy year. Co-payment 20% of each admissible claim treated in a Zone B city.
Hospitalization means admission to a Hospital for at least 24 consecutive hours.
Day Care Treatment means a procedure completed in under 24 hours.
Pre-existing Disease means a condition diagnosed within 36 months before cover began.
In-patient Hospitalization: up to Sum Insured. Subject to Clause 1.1.
Room rent: 1% of Sum Insured per day. Proportionate deduction applies if exceeded.
Intensive care unit: 2% of Sum Insured per day. Medically necessary admission only.
Pre-hospitalization: 60 days before admission. Related to the admitted condition.
Post-hospitalization: 90 days after discharge. Related to the admitted condition.
Day care treatment: up to Sum Insured. As defined in Clause 1.2.
Cataract surgery: INR 50,000 per eye. Sub-limit applies per policy year, and counts towards the Sum Insured. See waiting period in Clause 3.2.
Maternity: INR 60,000 per delivery. Sub-limit applies per policy year, and counts towards the Sum Insured. After the waiting period in Clause 3.4.
Newborn cover: INR 25,000. Covered with Clause 2.8.
Ambulance: INR 3,000 per Hospitalization. Registered ambulance services only.
AYUSH treatment: INR 25,000 per policy year. In a government-recognized hospital.
Organ donor expenses: INR 1,00,000. Recipient must be an Insured Person.
Domiciliary treatment: 10% of Sum Insured. Only where the patient cannot be moved.
Health check-up: INR 5,000 every two policy years. No claim needed in the preceding period.
No claim is payable in the first 30 days of cover, except for accidents.
Cataract, hernia, and kidney stones: 24 months.
Cosmetic treatment, except reconstruction following an accident or burns.
Obesity treatment, unless the conditions of Clause 4.3 are met.
Bariatric surgery is covered only when BMI is 40 or above.
Dental treatment, except when needed because of an accident.

Treatment received outside India is not covered. This exclusion applies to every benefit in Section 2, including Hospitalization, day care treatment, ambulance, and AYUSH treatment, whether the treatment was planned or arose during travel. shield: Plan: Comprehensive Health Shield. Sum Insured INR 15,00,000 per policy year on a floater basis. Co-payment: 15% of each admissible claim for Insured Persons who enter the policy at age 60 or above. Deductible: nil. Room category: single private air-conditioned room. Cumulative bonus: 10% of the base Sum Insured for each claim-free year, up to 50%.
Accident means a sudden, unforeseen, and involuntary event caused by external, visible, and violent means.

AYUSH Hospital means a healthcare facility registered for Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, or Homeopathy treatment, with at least 5 in-patient beds and qualified practitioners available around the clock.
Cashless Facility means a facility under which the Insurer pays a Network Provider directly for treatment approved in advance, up to the amount authorized.

Day Care Treatment means medical or surgical treatment under general or local anaesthesia, in a Hospital or day care centre, in less than 24 hours because of technological advancement, which would otherwise have needed Hospitalization of more than 24 hours.

Domiciliary Hospitalization means medical treatment for more than three days, for an illness that would normally need care in a Hospital, taken at home because the patient cannot be moved, or because no Hospital bed is available.

Hospital means an institution registered with the local authorities for in-patient care, with qualified nursing staff around the clock, at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with fewer than ten lakh people and 15 elsewhere, a fully equipped operation theatre, and daily records of patients.
Intensive Care Unit means an identified section of a Hospital, under the constant supervision of a dedicated Medical Practitioner, for critically ill patients needing continuous monitoring.
Medical Practitioner means a person registered with a medical council in India to practise medicine within the scope of that licence. It does not include the Insured Person or a close family member.

Medically Necessary treatment means treatment that is required for the medical management of the illness or injury, does not exceed the level of care needed, is prescribed by a Medical Practitioner, and conforms to accepted medical practice in India.
Network Provider means a Hospital enlisted by the Insurer or its administrator to provide treatment through the Cashless Facility.

Pre-existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury, or disease that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was recommended by or received from a physician, within 36 months before the first policy issued by the Insurer.
Reasonable and Customary Charges means the charges for services or supplies that are standard for the area, for similar services, considering the nature of the illness or injury involved.
Co-payment means the share of each admissible claim that the Insured Person bears, as a percentage stated in the Schedule. It does not reduce the Sum Insured.
Cumulative Bonus means the increase in Sum Insured granted on renewal for each claim-free policy year, as stated in the Schedule.

The Insurer covers medical expenses for Hospitalization for more than 24 hours for an illness or injury during the policy period, including room, boarding, and nursing; Intensive Care Unit charges; surgeon, anaesthetist, consultant, and specialist fees; anaesthesia, blood, oxygen, operation theatre, drugs, and surgical appliances; and diagnostic tests, up to the Sum Insured.

Room rent is payable up to the room category in the Schedule. If the Insured Person stays in a higher room category, all associated medical expenses, except medicines, consumables, and implants, are paid in the proportion that the eligible room rent bears to the room rent actually incurred.
Medical expenses incurred in the 60 days before admission are covered, if they relate to the same condition and the Hospitalization claim is admissible.
Medical expenses incurred in the 90 days after discharge are covered, if they relate to the same condition and the Hospitalization claim is admissible.
Day Care Treatment is covered up to the Sum Insured, for the procedures listed in Annexure B.

Domiciliary Hospitalization is covered up to 10% of the Sum Insured. It does not cover asthma, bronchitis, chronic nephritis, diarrhoea, epilepsy, hypertension, influenza, arthritis, gout, or psychiatric disorders.
In-patient AYUSH treatment in an AYUSH Hospital is covered up to the Sum Insured.
Expenses of a registered road ambulance to the nearest Hospital, or between Hospitals for better care, are covered up to INR 3,000 per Hospitalization.
In-patient expenses of an organ donor for harvesting an organ for an Insured Person are covered up to the Sum Insured. Pre- and post-hospitalization expenses of the donor are not covered.

The following are covered up to 25% of the Sum Insured each, for in-patient or day care treatment: (a) robotic surgeries; (b) stereotactic radiosurgery; (c) oral chemotherapy; (d) immunotherapy by monoclonal antibody injection; (e) intravitreal injections; (f) balloon sinuplasty; (g) deep brain stimulation; (h) uterine artery embolization; (i) stem cell therapy for haematological conditions only.
In-patient treatment of mental illness is covered up to the Sum Insured, in a Hospital with a psychiatric unit, under a psychiatrist.
Bariatric surgery is covered up to INR 2,00,000 per policy year, if the body mass index is 40 or above, or 35 or above with a severe co-morbidity, and conservative treatment has failed.
If the Sum Insured and Cumulative Bonus are used up in a policy year, the Sum Insured is restored once in that year, for a later claim for a different illness.
A health check-up is reimbursed up to INR 5,000 once every policy year, whether or not a claim was made.
Expenses for any illness contracted within 30 days of the first policy start date are not covered. This does not apply to treatment needed because of an Accident.

Expenses for the following are covered only after 24 months of continuous cover: (a) cataract; (b) benign prostatic hypertrophy; (c) hernia and hydrocele; (d) kidney and gall bladder stones; (e) fissure, fistula, and piles; (f) sinusitis and tonsillitis; (g) knee and hip joint replacement, unless needed because of an Accident; (h) varicose veins; (i) bariatric surgery.
Expenses for Pre-existing Diseases and their direct complications are covered only after 36 months of continuous cover since the first policy.

Where the Insured Person had continuous health cover with any Indian insurer before this policy, the waiting periods in Clauses 3.2 and 3.3 are reduced by the length of that earlier cover, up to the earlier sum insured.

Cosmetic or plastic surgery, or any treatment to change appearance, is excluded, unless it is reconstruction following an Accident, burns, or cancer, or is part of Medically Necessary treatment certified by the attending Medical Practitioner.
Dental treatment, dentures, and dental implants are excluded, unless needed because of an Accident and requiring Hospitalization.
Spectacles, contact lenses, hearing aids, and cochlear implants are excluded, as are vision correction procedures for a refractive error of less than 7.5 dioptres.

Treatment of injuries from participation in hazardous or adventure sports, such as para-jumping, rock climbing, mountaineering, motor racing, scuba diving, and bungee jumping, is excluded, unless the sport is the Insured Person's profession.
Treatment of intentional self-injury, attempted suicide, or the abuse of alcohol, drugs, or other addictive substances, and its consequences, is excluded.
Admission primarily for diagnostic tests or evaluation, without active treatment for an illness found during the stay, is excluded.
Admission for custodial care, rest cure, rehabilitation, or respite care is excluded.
Treatment, services, or supplies that lack significant medical documentation of their effectiveness are excluded.
Treatment of infertility and sterility, including assisted reproduction such as in vitro fertilization, gamete transfer, and surrogacy, is excluded.
Expenses for childbirth, caesarean section, and pregnancy, including miscarriage and abortion, are excluded, except ectopic pregnancy treated as an emergency.
Treatment arising from war, invasion, acts of foreign enemies, civil war, or nuclear, chemical, or biological contamination is excluded.
Treatment taken outside India is excluded.
Items listed in Annexure A as non-medical, such as toiletries, attendant charges, admission kits, gloves, and food for visitors, are excluded.
The Insurer must be told of a planned Hospitalization at least 72 hours before admission, and of an emergency Hospitalization within 24 hours of admission.

For a Cashless Facility, the Network Provider sends a pre-authorization request with the Insured Person's identity card. The Insurer replies within one hour. Approval may be partial, and any difference is settled at discharge.

For reimbursement, submit within 30 days of discharge: the claim form, original bills and receipts, the discharge summary, investigation reports, prescriptions, and a cancelled cheque. Post-hospitalization claims are submitted within 15 days of completing that treatment.

The Insurer settles or rejects a claim within 30 days of receiving the last necessary document. If it is late, it pays interest at 2% above the bank rate, from the date the claim should have been settled.
A complaint may be made to the Insurer's grievance officer. If unresolved within 30 days, the Insured Person may approach the Insurance Ombudsman.
A new policy may be returned within 30 days of receipt, if no claim has been made. The premium is refunded after deducting expenses for medical examinations and stamp duty.
After 60 continuous months of cover, no claim may be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except for proven fraud.
The policy is renewable for life, except for fraud or misrepresentation. A grace period of 30 days is allowed for renewal, without cover for illness contracted during the grace period.
If a claim is fraudulent, or supported by a false statement or document, all benefits for that claim are forfeited, and amounts paid must be repaid.
An Insured Person may move this policy to another insurer at renewal, keeping credit for waiting periods already served, by applying at least 15 days before renewal.
The Insured Person may cancel the policy with 7 days' notice. The premium for the unexpired period is refunded on a short-period scale, if no claim has been made.
